The transcript discusses unaudited financial results for the quarter ended 30th September 2026. Management reported consolidated growth driven by innovation. Titan Jewellery recorded a customs duty gain of Rs. 490 crores, while CaratLane recorded Rs. 46 crores. Normalized margins were stated as 11.1% for Titan Jewellery and 11.7% after adjusting for mark-to-market reversals. Investment buying remained soft, while studded jewellery demand was strong. Lower caratage jewellery adoption continues as a strategic long-term initiative. The board has approved raising Rs. 2,500 crores for replenishing existing borrowing.

The framework promotes responsible copper production. It involves independent third-party audits of environmental, social, and governance performance. The order book stood at Rs.98.5 million with a book to bill ratio of 1.18x. AI-led orders contributed 24.2 million, representing 25% of the total order book. The company confirmed that customer The Children's Place filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States. Atraco Industrial Enterprise FZE holds outstanding receivables of USD 4.11 million associated with this customer. The Children's Place contributes approximately 5% to 6% of the company's consolidated total income. Management assesses a reasonably high probability of significant recovery of the outstanding receivables. The company is actively monitoring proceedings and taking legal and commercial steps to safeguard financial interests. Additionally, Gokaldas Exports onboarded two major new customers within its African manufacturing operations. These include one large U.S. retail customer and one prominent European customer. The company is reallocating capacity to scale production and deepen engagement with these new clients.

SANDUMA.attchmntText: Sandur Manganese & Iron Ores Limited has informed the Exchange regarding 'Grant of Environmental Clearance by Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change'.
SANDUMA.voiceSummary: The Sandur Manganese and Iron Ores Limited has received Environmental Clearance from the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. The clearance, identified by number EC26A0000KA5280635N dated 11 November 2026, permits the enhancement of iron ore Run of Mine capacity from 7.85 Million Tonnes Per Annum to 9.42 Million Tonnes Per Annum. It also allows for the reduction of manganese ore Run of Mine capacity from 1.34 Million Tonnes Per Annum to 0.7330 Million Tonnes Per Annum. The approval is based on the Indian Bureau of Mines approved mining plan for Mining Lease No.2678 within an area of 1860.10 hectares. The Beneficiation plant configuration will change from 1 x 7.00 to 2 x 3.5 Million Tonnes Per Annum. The Downhill Conveyor System remains unchanged. The company will initiate further regulatory approvals to operate at these enhanced levels.

IMFA.attchmntText: Indian Metals & Ferro Alloys Limited has informed the Exchange about Transcript
IMFA.voiceSummary: Indian Metals and Ferro Alloys Limited filed the transcript of its Q2 and H1 FY27 earnings conference call held on 4th November 2026. The board approved the unaudited financial results for the quarter and half year ended 30th September 2026. Managing Director Subhrakant Panda reported higher performance due to capacity additions and better prices. The KNR-2 unit reached 84,000 tons per annum production, with full capacity expected by December 2026. The KNR-1 unit achieved hot metal tapping on 25th August 2026, with the second furnace expected around 15th November 2026. The company approved a capex of INR375 crores to increase chrome ore output and produce low-carbon ferro chrome. Volume guidance for FY27 remains at 380,000 tons, and FY28 at 475,000 tons.
